title: Skip screen digitizers when detecting the touchpad
head: 3318b310013c
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Hyprland's duplicate-name suffix lets a screen digitizer evade the exclusion
leads.consequence: When two screen mouse nodes normalize to the same *-touchpad name, Hyprland calls the later one *-touchpad-1. The filter strips only a terminal -touchpad/-trackpad, so after skipping the first screen it returns the second screen ahead of the keyboard-cover touchpad. The menu remains visible, but toggling it disables the screen and persists the wrong name. On the next reload default/hypr/disabled-input-device.lua disables that same saved screen device again. Support optional numeric collision suffixes in pairing, with cases for two identically named screens and a cover.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N3); corroboration noted

leads.summary: Existing screen disable state cannot be restored by the new detector
leads.consequence: A user who toggled the mistakenly detected screen off before upgrading already has its *-touchpad mouse name in touchpad-disabled-name. After the new filter selects the keyboard cover, `omarchy toggle touchpad on` removes that saved screen name but calls `hl.device(enabled=true)` for the cover only, never for the disabled screen. The default toggle likewise takes the enable branch while the file exists. The old screen remains disabled in the running Hyprland session, and after the file is removed no retry via toggle can target it; a compositor reload/device reconnect is needed to restore its default. Consider restoring the saved device as well when enabling, then clearing the state, or explicitly migrate affected saved names.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2); corroboration noted

leads.summary: Related open touchpad detector PRs cannot merge without composing their logic and tests
leads.consequence: Open #8281 and #13362 independently replace the detector and also add the same test path; #12307 replaces the detector too. None is stacked with this head. The file merges have conflict markers; simply selecting this PR's detector drops udev-only pads or internal-pad priority, whereas selecting the other detector drops digitizer exclusion, causing this PR's cover fixture to return the first screen. Their test suites fail against this head, and both same-path test files need to be retained in a combined suite. Resolve by applying classification and priority AFTER removing digitizer matches, preserving the udev fallbacks and all tests. #9218 and #7488 also edit the same regex line and need their new alternatives kept if integrated.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q5); corroboration noted

leads.summary: Negative fixtures assert failure status but not absence of an incorrectly printed name
leads.consequence: Both negative cases discard stdout and stderr and pass on any nonzero status. A detector that prints a digitizer or mouse name before returning 1 satisfies the tests even though `omarchy hw touchpad` leaks a wrong device name to CLI users or any output-consuming caller. Assert stdout is empty as well as the intended exit status (and use a separate check for jq errors), especially for the digitizers-only fixture.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q4 minor); not published: no demonstrated surviving mutant

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found for the reported dual-screen case; three optional notes are collapsed below.

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- With synthetic `hyprctl devices -j` input shaped like Hyprland 0.56.2's output, the keyboard-cover pad is chosen over the digitizers' `*-touchpad` nodes, and nothing is printed (exit 1) when only digitizers are present.
- All 9 fixtures without a screen digitizer give the same stdout and exit status as before the change (jq 1.8.2).
- The new test fails against the pre-PR script (`actual: elan9008:00-04f3:4447-touchpad`) and passes at the head and on the current `quattro` base branch with the PR applied.
- Exit status is unchanged: the old `[[ -n $device ]] && echo` line already exited 1 with no device, and the menu `when` guard and `omarchy-toggle-input-device` handle it as before.
- Kernel naming (i2c-hid, hid-multitouch, hid-input) plus Hyprland's name normalisation makes a hid-multitouch digitizer's touchpad node `<touch name>-touchpad` (unless Hyprland adds a `-N` suffix, note 3), which is what the filter strips and matches.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

1. **Disable saved by the old detection is not undone.** If `touchpad-disabled-name` holds a digitizer node written before this change, `omarchy-toggle-touchpad on` (or toggle) deletes the file but sends `enabled = true` only for the newly detected pad, or fails with "No touchpad device found" when the cover is off. The digitizer node never receives `enabled = true`; whether it recovers at the next config reload was not tested. Benefit: users who hit the original bug get back, from the same toggle, the digitizer node the old detection disabled. Possible change: enable the saved name before clearing it (as open #12360 does), or add a one-shot migration.
2. **jq before 1.8 parses the filter differently.** jq 1.8.0 changed the precedence of `... as $x |` (jqlang/jq#3053). On jq 1.7.1 the filter errors whenever a pad is found, so no touchpad is ever reported. Omarchy's mirrors currently ship jq 1.8.2, so there is no current impact. `((.touch // []) + (.tablets // []) | map(.name)) as $digitizers` gave identical results on all 15 fixtures under jq 1.8.2 and the same results under jq 1.7.1. Benefit: detection keeps working on a system with an older jq.
3. **Hyprland's `-N` duplicate-name suffix is not stripped.** Hyprland appends `-1`, `-2` to a name another input device already holds, and `sub("-touchpad$|-trackpad$"; "")` does not match `...-touchpad-1`, so such a digitizer node is not skipped, and is selected when it is listed first. For I2C digitizers the ACPI instance (`:00`) normally keeps names unique, so this is an edge case. Benefit: the digitizer node would still be skipped if Hyprland renames it; allowing an optional `-N` after the stripped suffix was not tested.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: saved digitizer disable (note 1)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from a checkout of the PR head. Simulates a touchpad-disabled-name file
# written by the pre-PR detection (a screen digitizer's -touchpad node).
set -u
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr"
cat >"$tmp/bin/hyprctl" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
case $1 in
  devices) cat "$DEVICES" ;;
  eval) echo "hyprctl eval: $2" >&2 ;;
esac
STUB
printf '#!/bin/bash\n:\n' >"$tmp/bin/omarchy-osd"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/hyprctl" "$tmp/bin/omarchy-osd"
cat >"$tmp/cover-off.json" <<'JSON'
{"mice":[{"name":"elan9008:00-04f3:4447-touchpad"},{"name":"elan9009:00-04f3:4448-touchpad"}],
 "touch":[{"name":"elan9008:00-04f3:4447"},{"name":"elan9009:00-04f3:4448"}],"tablets":[]}
JSON
cat >"$tmp/cover-bt.json" <<'JSON'
{"mice":[{"name":"elan9008:00-04f3:4447-touchpad"},{"name":"asus-zenbook-duo-keyboard-touchpad"}],
 "touch":[{"name":"elan9008:00-04f3:4447"}],"tablets":[]}
JSON
state="$tmp/home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/touchpad-disabled-name"
for cover in cover-off cover-bt; do
  echo 'elan9008:00-04f3:4447-touchpad' >"$state"
  echo "== $cover, stale name file present"
  HOME="$tmp/home" DEVICES="$tmp/$cover.json" PATH="$tmp/bin:$PWD/bin:$PATH" bin/omarchy-toggle-touchpad on
  echo "exit=$? name_file=$([[ -e $state ]] && echo present || echo removed)"
done
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Actual output (sandboxed run):

```
== cover-off, stale name file present
No touchpad device found
exit=1 name_file=removed
== cover-bt, stale name file present
hyprctl eval: hl.device({ name = "asus-zenbook-duo-keyboard-touchpad", enabled = true })
exit=0 name_file=removed
```

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: jq 1.7.1 (note 2)</summary>

```bash

cat >"$tmp/hyprctl" <<'STUB'

echo '{"mice":[{"name":"elan-internal-touchpad"}],"keyboards":[],"tablets":[],"touch":[],"switches":[]}'
STUB
chmod +x "$tmp/hyprctl"

echo "== $(jq --version)"

rm -rf "$tmp"

```

elan-internal-touchpad
exit=0

jq: error (at <stdin>:1): array ([]) and string ("elan-inter...) cannot be added

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: -N suffix (note 3, test case appended to the PR's test file)</summary>

```bash
write_devices <<'JSON'
{
  "mice": [
    {"name": "elan9008:00-04f3:4447-touchpad-1"},
    {"name": "asus-zenbook-duo-keyboard-touchpad"}
  ],
  "touch": [
    {"name": "elan9008:00-04f3:4447"}
  ],
  "tablets": []
}
JSON
device=$(hw_touchpad)
[[ $device == "asus-zenbook-duo-keyboard-touchpad" ]] ||
  fail "a digitizer pad with Hyprland's -N duplicate suffix is skipped" "actual: $device"
pass "a digitizer pad with Hyprland's -N duplicate suffix is skipped"
```

Actual output:

```
ok - a lone laptop touchpad is used
ok - a keyboard cover trackpad wins over screen digitizers
ok - screen digitizers alone are not a trackpad
ok - an internal pad still wins when a keyboard pad is also present
ok - a trackpad name is used
ok - a plain mouse is not a trackpad
actual: elan9008:00-04f3:4447-touchpad-1
not ok - a digitizer pad with Hyprland's -N duplicate suffix is skipped
exit=1
```

</details>

<details><summary>Related open PRs</summary>

- #8281 and #13362 also add `test/shell.d/hw-touchpad-test.sh` (add/add conflict) and replace the same selector line; #12307, #9218 and #7488 also rewrite that jq line.
- #8281 and #13362 fall back to udev `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD` when the name match returns nothing. After this PR that includes the digitizers-only case, so a combination could select a digitizer node through udev if udev tags it as a touchpad (not verified on hardware).
- #12307 prefers a single udev-internal pad and does not skip digitizers, so combining it with this PR would need the digitizer filter applied to its candidates.
</details>
